headline: High-risk shared filesystem and git state create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error pathways between Gemini CLI and Superset.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run with user-approved tools; its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Superset exposes an API and allowlisted egress, so if Gemini writes attacker-controlled content into shared files that Superset later ingests, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI writes untrusted content into a shared workspace that Superset later reads as instructions or config
IF Superset ingests file-backed content without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers not strictly needed
Require provenance tags on shared files
Review any file-to-API ingestion path before use

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; Superset has allowlisted egress and an API surface. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, Gemini can read them and potentially transmit them, while Superset may also expose derived data through its API. The profiles do not show isolation or DLP by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared cwd or repo
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to send file contents to external services
IF Superset API responses include derived sensitive fields
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared workspace
Restrict Gemini egress to approved endpoints
Mask sensitive columns before Superset exposure
Use separate service accounts and credentials

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and git-state modification; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Superset exposes an API and allowlisted network egress. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt files or git state, and no locking mechanism is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Superset or its automation writes artifacts that Gemini also edits
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Add a file-locking wrapper
Serialize write operations through one orchestrator
Run one agent read-only during the other's write phase

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell commands, and file edits; Superset can consume API-driven inputs and produce analytics artifacts. If Superset treats Gemini output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into dashboards, configs, or downstream actions. The profiles do not show a validation gate, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Gemini-generated files, SQL, or config without review
IF Gemini output is used as the source of truth for analytics or deployment steps
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Validate generated SQL/config against schemas
Require tests before applying changes
Limit Gemini to draft-only outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are stated for either profile, and both are open-source. The only concrete compliance concern is that Gemini CLI handles shell environment and files in cwd, which could conflict with local policy if regulated data is placed there. Superset is not shown to receive such data by default, so the gap is limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared cwd or repo
IF local policy requires stricter handling than the current workspace provides
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use a policy-approved sandbox
Rotate any exposed secrets
Document retention and deletion steps
